sections.title: Sound of equis
paragraphs: The letter is named (equis) /ˈekis/. Its main sound appears in (xilófono) /siˈlofono/, which means xylophone. This letter can make three sounds.

sections.title: How to say equis
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Release the air, then push air over the tongue tip behind your teeth. For the next sound, hiss air smoothly behind your upper teeth. For the last sound, raise the back of your tongue near the soft roof. Push air through the small gap with a strong friction. Put a hand on your throat. Your voice stays off for every sound.

sections.title: Spelling of equis
paragraphs: Between vowels or at the end of a word, say both consonants together. You hear this sound in (éxito) /ˈeksito/ and in (tórax) /ˈtoɾaks/. At the start of a word, it sounds like a simple hiss. You hear that sound in (xilófono) /siˈlofono/. Before another consonant, it also makes a hiss, as in (texto) /ˈtesto/. In traditional place names, it sounds like a rough throat sound. You hear this in (México) /ˈmexiko/ and in (Don Quixote) /doŋ kiˈxote/.

sections.title: Pitfalls with equis
paragraphs: Do not turn the sound into a voiced buzz like the x in exam. Keep your throat quiet and say a clean hiss like six. Do not say an English h in names like (México) /ˈmexiko/. Make a rasping sound from the back of the mouth instead.
